# Revenue model output (Canada, FY2024-25 worked example)

All amounts are $ billions, federal government, fiscal year April 2024 to March 2025.

**Incidence assumption.** Every scenario, static included, is computed under one stated assumption about prices and nominal spending. **A (central): real base fixed** - the VAT is passed into prices and households keep buying the same tax-exclusive basket, so revenue on today's base = rate x base. **B (sensitivity): nominal spending fixed** - prices rise but nominal spending on today's base does not, so revenue = rate/(1+rate) x spending. "Dynamic" differs from "static" only by the extra spending from the income tax people keep; that new spending buys rate-inclusive goods under both A and B.

Effective (net) base = net GST / 5% = 1050.1. Gross base = gross GST / 5% = 1175.4. PIT + CIT = 10.8% of GDP. Core need (PIT + CIT + net GST) = **383.8**; full federal scope (adds non-resident tax and EI premiums) = **428.8**.

## Table 5. Dynamic scenario: households keep the income tax and spend it

All 331.3 of PIT + CIT stays with households and firms. A share (MPC) is spent; a share of that spending (taxable share = 0.61) lands in the VAT base and pays rate-inclusive prices. Imports (32.7% of GDP) do not leak from a destination-based base; they matter only for the multiplier. "+ mult" adds Finance Canada's short-run multipliers (PIT 1.0, CIT 0.3). MPC 0.000 is the static case.

| A | The prebate costs about as much as all of today's direct program expenses | net $233.0B a year against $237.6B [R2] |
| B | The land value is not verified, so the LVT may raise much less | if the LVT raised nothing, B's rate would be A's: 36.2% |
| B | Provinces and municipalities already tax property | the LVT must first replace $92.6B of property tax (§5.4) |
| C | Wealth is hard to value and mobile; the PBO already cuts the base by 35% for avoidance | VAT 31.2% with it, 32.6% without it |
| All | With PIT at zero, the deemed disposition at death goes with it, so gains never realised are never taxed | only the VAT on what the owners spend, and package C's wealth tax, reach them |
| All | Retirees who saved out of taxed income pay VAT again when they spend | see the retiree row in §13.4 |
